## Pass 1

Changes are listed as unit · field · severity · what was wrong · what was done. Units are numbered from 0, as in units.json. All edits were made by script (/tmp/claude-0/reviewer017a/edit.py, plus one small follow-up edit in U28). Each script asserts the old value before it replaces it. No glyph code, glyph order, rubric flag or restored flag was changed.

- U24, U28 · words[ꜥbꜣ], words[ꜥbꜣ·n·f] (reading, say, glyphs, morph, n) · major · The O26 + N29 pair was read ꜥbꜣ 'fight (?)' and coded O26 phon "ꜥb", G1 phon. That made a new lemma. Published ani-001-a reads the same pair, followed by the same vulture and low sign, as ꜥḥꜣ 'fight' (O26 phon ꜥḥꜣ, N29 det, G1 comp ꜣ, U15 det). Nothing in the signs here rules that reading out · reading → ꜥḥꜣ / ꜥḥꜣ·n·f, say → aha / ahanef, O26 tr → "ꜥḥꜣ", G1 role → comp, lemma → ꜥḥꜣ (known). The U24 note now follows ani-001-a: the pair is read ꜥḥꜣ as in Spell 1, U15 is the forearm-with-stick classifier of force, Budge has āba although no sign of the pair can be identified as b or ḥ, and the reading is not sure. U28 refers back to it.
- U27 · words[n] + words[[…]] → n·i; l, i, n · major · The lone kneeling man after n (Budge's '. . .') was left as an unread word with the lemma "[…]", and the clause was given as 'which Ra gave to […]'. The seated man is the first-person suffix. A pronoun dative comes before a noun subject, so rdi n·i rꜥ is regular: 'which Ra gave to me' · The two words are joined as n·i (N35 phon n, A1 suff ·i; q "0-1"; morph n, ·i; say "eni", as in the published parts). l "gave · to-me · Ra"; i "…, which Ra gave to me." The note says that Budge prints them as two words, names the form (the relative form of rdi with Ra as subject) and calls the reading likely but not sure. In the same note, "no word nnw fits" claimed too much. It now says that D41 classifies words of inertness such as nni 'be weary', but that nnw cannot be confirmed here, and the word is still shown as […].
- U28 · l, i, n · major · ꜥḥꜣ·n·f is labelled a sḏm·n·f in the note, but l and i rendered it as a present tense ("fights-he", "he stands and fights for it"). ꜥḥꜥ had no form label · l "has-fought-he"; i "When any god goes down into it, he takes his stand: he has fought for it." The note now calls ꜥḥꜥ a sḏm·f whose subject, the god, is not repeated. It names the sḏm·n·f as the completed action and gives the narrative ꜥḥꜥ·n sḏm·n·f 'then he fought' (with the n of ꜥḥꜥ·n unwritten) as an alternative.
- U0 · l, i, n · minor · sṯs was rendered "the-praises" / "praises", which is Budge's 'praisings'. Published ani-001-a renders the same word in the same title "raising up" and gives Budge's word only in the note · l "raising-up · glorifications"; i "The beginning of raising up and glorification, …". The note now reads "sṯs 'raising up, extolling' (Budge: seθes, 'praisings') … as in the title of Spell 1".
- U0 · n · style · ꜣḫt 'being glorious' did not mention that Spell 1 reads the same word in the same title as the adjective 'glorious' qualifying the necropolis · added: Spell 1's reading is also possible. The draft's reading is kept, because here the red ends before the word. The phrase "the compound that heads a book or a list" was trimmed so that the note stays under the limit (1568 characters).
- U0, U1, U2 · l, i, n (prt) · style · pri was rendered "going out". The published parts (001-a, 022-072) use "going forth" for the same infinitive in the same formula · → "going forth" / "going-forth".
- U0 · words[nfrt] glyph Z9 role · minor · The horns Z9 were coded phon with empty tr, but the viper next to them is comp f. The 022-072 ruling gives the horns the viper's own role · role → comp (tr stays empty).
- U4 · words[ir-s] · minor · Two words, the participle ir and the dependent pronoun s, were joined under one hyphenated reading. A hyphen marks a compound, which this is not · split into ir (D4 phon, D21 comp; q "0:1"; lemma ir) and s (O34 phon z; say "es"; lemma st, as the published parts code the dependent pronoun). The note says that Budge's group is split.
- U5, U6, U17 · morph lemma tm → itm · minor · Atum was filed under "tm", a key that would collide with the verb tm. Neither key exists in known-lemmas · lemma → itm. The reading stays tm, since the reed is not written, as the U5 note says.
- U12 · words[psḏt] glyph X6 role; n · minor · X6 was coded phon, and the note argued psḏt from scratch, calling it doubtful against Budge's paut. The published Weighing of the Heart reads X6 + t as psḏt three times, with X6 coded log psḏ · role → log. The note now cites that reading and keeps the doubt only about the identification of the sign in the print.
- U14 · l, i, n · minor · ḫpr nn pw was rendered "came-into-being · these · (pw)", with pw "a demonstrative not translated". This is a sentence with pw: 'it is the coming into being of these' · l "coming-into-being · of-these · it-is"; i "…; that is the coming into being of these, as the gods who are in the following of Ra." The note explains the pw sentence.
- U14 · words[ḫt] morph gloss · minor · An inline gloss "rear, following (noun; …)" was given for a fourth homonym of ḫt. A new sense of a known lemma belongs in the glossary (`__broaden__`), not in the morph · inline gloss removed. **Glosser:** broaden ḫt with "a fourth word: rear, following (noun; m-ḫt 'after', imyw-ḫt 'those in the following of', the retinue)".
- U22 · words[sḥtm] glyph Q1 role / tr; n · minor · The stepped seat sign was coded phon "t" and the note said it "is read t". The seat has no t value, and the published Hymn to Ra codes the same sign in sḥtm as a classifier (Q1 det) · role → det, tr → "". The note now says that neither t nor m of ḥtm is printed and that the seat is a classifier, as in the Hymn to Ra. The doubt stays.
- U23 · words[iw·n] glyph Z2 role · minor · The plural strokes after the water n of ·n were coded suff with empty tr. Every published ·n, ·tn and ·sn codes the strokes det · role → det.
- U23 · n · style · No form was named for mn after iw·n · added: "its form after iw·n is not clear".
- part · minor · "the beginnings of the praises" is Budge's chapter title ('The beginnings of the praisings') · → "Spell 17, part 1 — the title and the first statements (Plate 7)".
- U33, about · words[bnw] say; l, i, n · style · "Benu" / say "Benu". The published parts and known-lemmas use "the Bennu" and say "benu" · → Bennu; say "benu".

### Refused findings
- tr coding (U8, U13, U16, U20, U25, U30, U35: X1 comp t, D21 comp r, M17 phon i, M6 phon tr, A2 det): the task asks whether t and r can be complements of M6. They stand before the sign, not after it. Complements before the main sign are normal in this hand (X1 before the sledge in tm, U6/U17, and N29 before T14 in qmꜣ). The coding is the same, sign for sign, as published ani-125-address U38 (pw tr) and as trwy in ani-001-b, and the note says the reed is not read. Kept for consistency.
- U10 qꜣqꜣ, Z9 det with empty tr: no viper stands beside it. The established file calls it an unidentified barred sign over a stroke, coded Z9 as an approximation, so the horns ruling does not apply. det is right, and the note marks it as unidentified. Kept.
- U24 wḏ·n, with the stroke and the seated man as det after the ·n: the published parts code the strokes of ·n, ·tn and ·sn as det. The man is an unusual classifier for a pronoun, but the note gives the alternative (a sḏm·n·f, 'when Osiris gave command') and marks the doubt. Kept.
- U3 m-ḫt, with F32 phon "ḫ" and Aa1 comp ḫ: the note explains that the belly stands for ḫ. This is a known exchange, and it accounts for every sign. Kept.
- U29, the second D21 coded phon "r" and not read: the note opens "The papyrus writes … read rḫ·kwi", following the misprint rule and house practice (022-072 E23 in šnꜥ·tw·f). Kept.
- U22 ḫftyw·f, the vulture ꜣ "has no place": it may be a slip or a variant spelling, and that cannot be settled. The note says so and does not claim a slip. Kept.
- U2 bꜣ, with G29 phon (001-b codes log): the hymns code it phon. The published parts are mixed, so no change.
- U6 m wn, U7 ḥqꜣ pn n·f, U10 m wnt n ḫpr, U23 dhn·n·tw / qrs, U26 st-imntt, U38 stꜣt·f and the stray n, U39 n r: every doubt is marked in the note and in l / i, and each reading accounts for the signs at least as well as any alternative I could build from them. Kept.
- p:true on the red questions: this follows the 022-072 practice (red section openings carry p). Kept.
- Restored flags: the packet flags all of w107 (qmꜣ) and w128 (tm) as restored, but the established file's own note puts only the owl G17 inside Budge's brackets. The draft flags G17 alone in both words, which is the more exact choice. Kept.
- Lemmas ky, dwꜣw: ky (with the known ḏd) is a separate lemma, as the other parts treat particles. dwꜣw 'tomorrow' is a different word from the known dwꜣ 'praise', so it is rightly new.
- Budge-isms and remembered wording: no "saith", "homage", "triumphant", "thee" or "draughts" in l / i. "after he has moored", "I am Yesterday; I know Tomorrow" and "As for Eternity, it is the day" follow directly from the grammar (m-ḫt + sḏm·f; ink N, stative; ir X pw Y). Kept.

For the glosser, beyond the new lemmas: qrs (known only as the verb 'bury') is used in U23 as a noun 'burial'. nk carries "(here) fornicate", which is pinned to Spell 125, and U32 needs the general sense. st is used in U4 for the dependent pronoun written with s alone. Each of these needs a `__broaden__`.

Re-check after editing: units.json parses and keeps its formatting (indent 1). The 951 sign codes, in order across all units, equal the packet's w0..w299. Every morph covers each glyph index of its word exactly once. Every det has an empty tr. Rubric flags match the packet glyph for glyph. Restored flags are unchanged: only G17 in U14 qmꜣ and U17 tm, as discussed above. The longest note is 1568 characters. The validator will warn about horns Z9 with empty tr in phon (rf, sf, ḫft, itf·f, ḫftyw·f) and in comp (nfrt). This is deliberate: the horns take the role of the viper they belong to.

## Pass 2

Changes are listed as U<n>/gloss · field · severity · what was wrong · what was done. Units are numbered from 0. All edits were made by script (/tmp/claude-0/reviewer017b/edit.py), and the script asserts each old value before it replaces it. No glyph code, glyph order, rubric flag or restored flag was changed.

- U28 · n · minor · ꜥḥꜥ was called "a sḏm·f whose subject, the god, is not repeated". A sḏm·f cannot stand without its subject · it is now taken as the stative with its ending unwritten, 'he (is) standing', with the god as subject. The alternative ꜥḥꜥ(·n) sḏm·n·f is kept.
- U5 · n · minor · ḏdt nbt tm was called "the direct genitive". nbt stands between the two nouns, where a direct genitive allows nothing · the note now says that tm is taken as a genitive with no n written, and that the construction is not sure.
- U18 · n · minor · iꜣbty was called "feminine to agree with ꜣḫt", but the reading shown, iꜣbty, is the masculine form. The t may equally be the t of iꜣbt 'east' · the note now says that the writing cannot show which it is.
- U10 · n · minor · wnt was called "an infinitive of wnn". The infinitive of wnn has no t · now "taken as a form of wnn 'be', though its t is not explained" (the construction was already marked doubtful). "written like sṯs 'praises'" still carried the rendering that pass 1 replaced · now "sṯs 'raising up'".
- U22 · n · minor · "ḥnꜥ sḥqꜣ·tw" was presented without doubt, but ḥnꜥ before a verb form is unusual · added: Budge takes the word as a noun ('the appointment as prince'), and the construction is not sure. The label of nw, "the plural genitive: 'those of'", was sharpened to "the genitive adjective in its plural form, agreeing with ḫftyw", with the reason for the rendering 'those of'.
- U32 · words[nk·f] morph gloss · minor · The known entry nk carries "(here) fornicate / commit adultery", which is pinned to Spell 125 and would be the gloss of Ra's act here. The glosser's __broaden__ only repeated "to copulate" · the broaden is dropped, and this occurrence has its own morph gloss "to copulate (verb)".
- U33 bnw, U39 nḥḥ · glyph N35 role · style · Water n was coded phon before the pot nw and the guinea fowl nḥ, which already carry n. That would spell bnnw and nnḥḥ · role → comp (tr stays n).
- U27 · l · style · rdi is the relative form ('which Ra gave to me'), but l showed only "gave" · → "which-gave".
- about · style · "the power to go out and come in" does not match the title, which gives prt and hꜣyt, 'going forth' and 'going down' · → "the power to go forth by day in any form and to go down into the necropolis".
- gloss __broaden__ st · minor · The addition repeated a pronoun sense already in the known entry ("it, them … written s-t") as a third item · now the known entry whole + " · the dependent pronoun is also written with s alone".
- gloss __broaden__ qrs · minor · "burial (noun; qrst; Budge: qeres, 'dead body')" mixed the lemma with Budge's sense of this occurrence. The units keep reading and lemma qrs (U23), and the note reads it as qrst with its t unwritten · now the known entry + " · qrst, burial (noun f.; the t is sometimes not written)".
- gloss __broaden__ ḫt · style · The new sense was added without marking it as a separate word, as the known entry does for the second and third words · " · a fourth word: rear, following (noun; …)".
- gloss __broaden__ ꜣḫ (new) · minor · U4 reads ꜣḫt as the noun 'something effective, a benefit'. No sense of the known entry covers it · added the known entry + " · also ꜣḫt, what is effective or useful, a benefit (noun f.)".
- gloss nnw · minor · "a word not identified (?)" had no grammar, and the "(?)" doubled the doubt · now "an unidentified word (word class unknown; the reading of the signs is doubtful; Budge renders 'that')".
- gloss ḥnn, stꜣt · style · Each carried notes about the classifiers or a sign of this occurrence ("the second sign is doubtful", "the classifiers are doubtful") · dropped. ḥnn now gives its spelling ḥnnw. stꜣt keeps its doubt about reading and sense.
- gloss šꜣꜥ, ḏs, sṯsw · style · Genders that cannot be confirmed (m.) were dropped. sṯsw no longer says "sṯs 'praises'" (the known entry is 'raise up'), and šꜣꜥ also mentions the verb 'to begin'.
- gloss ẖꜣt · style · Budge's spelling is not needed for a common noun · "corpse, dead body (noun f.)".

### Refused findings
- The tr coding of the question (X1/D21 complements before M6, the reed coded phon "i" and not read): pass 1's ruling stands. It follows published ani-125-address and ani-001-b.
- The coding of the double reed (phon "i i" here, "y y" in some published words): the published parts are mixed (both codings occur in 022-072, 001-a, 001-b and 125-address). No change.
- U19 "I am Yesterday; I know Tomorrow", U33 "I am that Bennu which is in Heliopolis": the wording follows directly from ink N + stative and from ink N pwy nty m X. It is not a borrowing. Kept.
- U6 m wn, U7 ḥqꜣ pn n·f, U23 iw·n mn / dhn·n·tw, U24 wḏ·n, U26 st-imntt, U27 nnw, U38 stꜣt·f and the stray n, U39 n r: each doubt is marked in the note and in l / i, and I could not build a reading from the signs that does better. Kept.
- U23 qrs: the reading stays qrs, as the signs give it, and is not changed to qrst. A t left unwritten is ordinary spelling, not a slip under the misprint rule. The note gives qrst.
- U14 ḫt 'rear': this stays a glossary broaden and does not become a separate lemma. The glossary keeps homonyms under one key, as the known entry ḫt already does.
- ḥbꜥ, znt, dhn, qꜣqꜣ, st-imntt, sipw, itm, mni, sḥ, sḥqꜣ, ky, dwꜣw: each has the right form, is general to its lemma, marks the doubt where the notes doubt it, and gives Budge's spelling where it is a name or a doubtful word. Kept.

Re-check: units.json and gloss.json parse, keep indent 1, and have no trailing newline, as before. The 951 sign codes, in order, equal the packet's w0..w299.
